newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria sup board meets on CA bid.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria sup board meets on CA bid.

text.p: Bank Austria said on Thursday its supervisory board was due to convene in the afternoon to consider adjustments to its bid for main rival Creditanstalt, whose privatisation is expected to be imminent.
A spokesman said the meeting would probably be concluded by 1800 local (1700 GMT). "It is not clear yet whether there will be a statement afterwards," he added.

Bank Austria has bid 16.8 billion schillings ($1.5 billion) for the state's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt, outbidding a rival consortium led by insurer EA-Generali by some three billion schillings.

According to a report in Thursday's edition of current affairs magazine News, Bank Austria was not expected to increase its offer. EA-Generali on Wednesday said it had improved its bid, but declined to say by how much.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima has given bidders a final deadline until Friday morning to update their offers for the country's flagship bank.

Sources close to the negotiations have tipped Bank Austria as the most likely winner in the privatisation battle, which has been dragged into its seventh year amid growing political controversy. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 11.09 Austrian Schillings)
